commands.name: offboard
commands.description: End this session with notes on what happened, what is relevant, and why it matters. You choose the stopping point. Run it last: the moment it returns, your seat has moved on to a fresh session. This session may finish what it is saying, but it receives nothing more and its junto commands are refused. At a stopping point: junto offboard "<notes>". The seat rests; its next wake starts a fresh session that reads your notes. Mid-work: junto offboard "<notes>" --continue "<note>". Junto starts the fresh session right away, and it reads your note first and carries on.

commands.name: create
description: Create an automation on an Automations node: a schedule, poll or change trigger, conditions in when, and actions in then. It is created off unless enabled is true, and runs on the machine named by machine, its short name, or else on the machine that rules the create. Targets are @name, #<task number> or a junto:// link, at or below the node and in your reach. A prompt action {kind: prompt, to: @seat, text} asks the seat to act, as junto msg send --prompt does; mail only tells it. An artifact watch {kind: artifact, artifact: <ref> or {node}, event: edited, commented or labelled, label?} fires on labelled when an artifact gains label (or a level under it), created with it included. Artifact actions: create-artifact {node, title, body?, labels?} makes a document from markdown; append-artifact {to, text} adds markdown at a document's end; label-artifact {to, add?, remove?} changes its labels, never one label in both. Their to is an artifact, or {fired: true}, the one that fired an artifact trigger. Labels fold to lowercase. A signal action {kind: signal, signal, title, detail?, show?, form?, id?, answerTo?} raises a signal in the operator's needs-you feed, from the automation, one per firing, never merged: escalate (a question, waiting on the operator), blocked, or feedback (asks for a review), each in the section a seat's would land in, or notice, only to read and clear. show names artifacts it opens. form, on escalate or blocked only, is what the operator answers in: {kind: text}, {kind: artifact, node, title?, labels?, minWords?} a document in that Artifacts node, titled from the signal unless named, of at least minWords,

or {kind: proof}. answerTo, never on notice, is where the answer goes: {kind: seat, to: @seat} prompts the seat with the signal and the answer; {kind: document, node, title} makes a new document in that Artifacts node, its title naming the step's own values and, said when the answer comes, {{answer.text}}, {{answer.link}}, {{answer.by}}, {{answer.at}}, {{signal.title}}, {{signal.kind}}, {{signal.link}}; {kind: append, to: <artifact>} appends a dated section. id names the step, 1 to 32 lower-case letters, digits and dashes, unique in the automation; a step with answerTo and no id gets one at save. A change watch {kind: answered, automation: {node, automationId}, step?, signal?} fires when the operator answers a signal that automation raised, on the same Automations node; step narrows to one signal step by its id, as junto automation show prints it (a step without one is given an id with automation edit first), and signal to escalate, blocked or feedback.

description.text: A secret answer is never a value, only its name.

A code step {kind: code, language: typescript or shell, file: ./step.ts, timeoutMs?} runs the program on the automation's machine: this command stages the file into the content store and sends its ref as source, so the code never rides the command line; only the operator and overseers write code.
